Task ID: 2-d
Agent: general-purpose
Task: Add a pytest drift guard (tests/test_docs_index.py) that keeps docs/INDEX.md in sync with the live pharmaml public API (implements R3 candidate e).

Work Log:
- Read worklog (R1–R3) + audited docs/INDEX.md (7 module sections, 62 symbol rows), scratch/build_docs_index.py and every documented module's `__all__`/dir() state; baseline suite re-run: 159 passed, 1 skipped.
- WROTE pharma-ml-toolkit/tests/test_docs_index.py (18 tests, Python only): markdown parser tolerant to formatting (any heading level, optional backticks, pipes inside summary cells via maxsplit=2, fenced code blocks skipped so the CLI section's pipe lines are not misread as table rows, header/alignment rows skipped) but strict about symbol names (valid identifiers only, no duplicate rows/sections, kinds limited to function/class/constant/module); package root located via `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent` → docs/INDEX.md so it works from the package dir, the repo root and any pytest rootdir (both verified); guarded `sys.path` insert of `src/` on top of pyproject's `pythonpath = ["src"]`; live-API rule = the module's `__all__` when declared, else public dir() names; kind check mirrors the generator (`inspect.isclass` → class, `isroutine or isfunction(unwrap)` → function — the R3 lru_cache fix for `molar_mass` is now regression-guarded, `ismodule` → module, else constant); a missing INDEX.md fails with the exact regeneration command (verified by temporarily moving the file away and back).
- DRIFT FOUND (first run: 2 of 18 tests failed): the `pharmaml.utils.io` and `pharmaml.utils.validation` sections of INDEX.md were EMPTY (header-only) while the live modules export 4 and 5 public functions. Root causes: (a) those were the only documented modules without an explicit `__all__`; (b) the generator used `getattr(mod, "__all__", [])` and silently emitted empty tables for `__all__`-less modules — latent since R1, and R2/R3 built the web API Reference on top without noticing.
- FIXED the root causes without weakening the test: added explicit `__all__` to src/pharmaml/utils/io.py (read_table, write_table, ensure_directory, safe_filename) and src/pharmaml/utils/validation.py (validate_positive, validate_smiles_syntax, require_columns, validate_concentration_series, coerce_frame) — matching the convention of every other module; fixed scratch/build_docs_index.py to fall back to public dir() names when `__all__` is absent (mirrors the test rule, so a future `__all__`-less module can never silently produce an empty section again).
- Regenerated docs/INDEX.md with `python scratch/build_docs_index.py` from the repo root: now 135 lines / 71 symbol rows — utils.io +4 function rows, utils.validation +5 function rows; the five `__all__`-based sections and the CLI section are byte-identical to before.
- Verified: full suite from pharma-ml-toolkit/ → 177 passed, 1 skipped; new module standalone and from a repo-root cwd → 18/18 passed; ruff line-length (≤100) clean; missing-INDEX.md error path prints the regeneration command.

Public API:
  * `smi_to_csv(smi_path, out_csv=None) -> Path` — streams rows as they are read (rar memory parity), columns SMILES/ID with whitespace-joined multi-word IDs (may be empty), blank lines skipped, utf-8-sig BOM output, default `<stem>.csv` beside the input, n-rows summary log, missing file → DataValidationError.
  * `table_to_sdf(data, out_sdf, *, smiles_col="SMILES", name_col=None, embed3d=True, uff=True, seed=0xF10E) -> SdfWriteReport` — every non-SMILES column becomes an SD tag (NaN cells simply not written); `_Name` = name_col value with 1-based-row-number fallback for empty/NaN cells, else rar-parity `ligand_{i}`; AddHs + ETKDG with fixed seed; embedding failure non-fatal (molecule kept without coordinates + note; UFF skipped); UFF convergence check non-fatal (note only); invalid SMILES counted + kept in `failed_smiles` (LigandLibrary accounting parity) and never written; scoped RDLogger suppression so parse errors land in the report instead of raw stderr; all-invalid or empty table → DataValidationError; rdkit missing → DependencyError.
  * `SdfWriteReport` @dataclass(slots=True) — source, output_sdf, molecules, failures, smiles_column, embedded_3d, notes, failed_smiles + LigandPreparationReport-style aligned `__str__` audit ("Table -> SDF conversion", note lines appended).
  * `sdf_to_table(sdf_path, out=None, smiles_col="SMILES") -> pd.DataFrame` — the Sdf reading.ipynb upgrade without PandasTools: one row per molecule with canonical SMILES, title → "name" column, every SD property as a typed column (SMILES+name ordered first); OSError → "empty or unreadable SDF" DataValidationError; all-None records → "no parseable molecules"; optional `out` written via write_table + logged.
  * `table_to_smi(data, out_smi, *, smiles_col="SMILES", name_col=None) -> Path` — inverse of smi_to_csv: "<smiles> <name>" lines, name omitted when no name_col or empty cell, blank SMILES cells skipped like blank .smi lines, validation mirrors smi_to_csv.
- Exported the 4 functions + SdfWriteReport from chem/__init__.py (same pattern as add_pic50_column; first docstring line kept a complete sentence so the INDEX blurb stays whole); chem blurb now "endpoint and file-format conversion, descriptors, similarity".
- CLI (src/pharmaml/cli.py): new `convert` subcommand under `data` — `--data` (.smi / .csv/.tsv/.xlsx / .sdf), `--to {csv,sdf,smi}`, `--smiles-col` (default SMILES), `--name-col` (default None → ligand_N titles), `--no-3d` (skip embed+UFF, table→sdf only), `--out` (default = input stem + target extension). `_cmd_data_convert` dispatches on (suffix, target): .smi→csv = smi_to_csv; →sdf = table_to_sdf(embed3d=not --no-3d) with a CLI-internal `_smi_bridge_frame` (.smi → SMILES/ID frame, so .smi→sdf works without the legacy two-step temp CSV); →smi = table_to_smi; .sdf→csv = sdf_to_table(out=...); .sdf→smi chains sdf_to_table + table_to_smi with automatic "name" column reuse; table→csv re-emits via read_table/write_table (xlsx/tsv shuffle). Bad combos are clear DataValidationErrors: .sdf→sdf ("already an SDF file -- use --to csv or --to smi"), .smi→smi. Prints the full SdfWriteReport audit + "output -> path" for sdf targets (failures → stderr note + exit 1, prep-ligands precedent) and compact "converted a -> b (n …)" lines otherwise. Registered ("data", "convert") in _HANDLERS; module docstring fence gains `pharmaml data convert --data ligands.csv --to sdf`.
- Tests: NEW tests/test_format_converters.py — 41 tests (importorskip rdkit gate, real SMILES fixtures CCO/c1ccccc1/aspirin/not_a_smiles): smi_to_csv (multi-word IDs joined, blank lines skipped, BOM bytes, missing file, custom out), table_to_sdf (DataFrame + CSV path sources, audit `__str__` alignment, SD-tag round-trip with typed values, name_col naming + empty-cell row-number fallback, default ligand_N naming, invalid accounting failures+failed_smiles, embed3d=False fast path still valid SDF, simulated ETKDG failure → fallback note + molecule still written, UFF non-convergence note, uff=False never calls UFF, all-invalid/empty-frame/missing-column errors, DependencyError via monkeypatch sys.modules {"rdkit": None, "rdkit.Chem": None}), sdf_to_table (out= writes table, missing/empty/unparseable SDF errors, DependencyError), table_to_smi (line format, name omitted without name_col, empty-name and blank-SMILES cells, error paths), CLI (csv→sdf --no-3d happy path with audit assertions, default out-path derivation, smi→csv, .smi→sdf bridge with --name-col ID, sdf→csv, csv→smi, invalid-SMILES exit 1 + stderr note, .sdf→sdf rejected, missing file exit 1).   1. HIGH — predict with FEWER feature columns than fitted silently BROADCAST: (n,1) X minus the (2,) per-feature mean pads to (n,2) in NumPy, so a 1-feature input returned full-shape GARBAGE predictions with no error (probe: 2-feature model, predict(X[:, :1]) -> (90,) output, all class 0); too MANY columns escaped as a raw numpy ValueError ("operands could not be broadcast"). MED — stratified val split stole single-member classes: _train_val_split only capped the per-class holdout when members.size > 1, so with val_split>=~0.6 a class with exactly ONE row landed entirely in the validation fold — the class vanished from TRAINING (probe: 3-class set, val_split=0.6 -> train classes {0,1}), violating the documented "every class keeps at least one training row". Fix: unconditional cap k = min(k, max(members.size - 1, 0)) (neural.py:487-489).
  4. MED — standardisation leaked the validation fold: _mean_/_std_ were computed over ALL rows passed to fit (comment claimed "fitted on the training block only"); probe planted a x500 outlier that landed in the VAL fold and dragged _mean_[0] from -0.18 (train-only) to +12.31 (full-data) — the early-stopping metric was computed on rows the scaler had seen. Fix: the split (seeded rng) now happens in fit() BEFORE scaling and mean/std use X_arr[train_idx] only; train_idx/val_idx/rng are threaded into _train_torch so the whole fit stays one deterministic random stream (neural.py:429-445).
  5. MED — y containing None escaped fit() as a RAW TypeError ("'<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and 'str'") from np.unique's sort. Fix: label encoding wrapped -> DataValidationError "classification targets could not be label-encoded ..." (neural.py:386-392).
  6. MED — a FAILED fit (torch missing) left a half-fitted estimator: classes_/n_features_in_/_mean_/_std_ were written before _require_torch(), so sklearn's check_is_fitted considered the estimator FITTED while predict raised "not fitted" (probe with sys.modules['torch']=None). LOW-MED — hidden_layers passed as a GENERATOR silently degenerated to a single linear layer: _validate_hyperparameters' loop consumed the generator, so _train_torch's tuple(...) saw () (probe: gen for (16,8) -> _net_spec_['hidden'] == ()). Agent: orchestrator (main conversation)
Task: Round 100x-34 of the 1000-round loop — the evaluate_model roc_auc column-inversion fix (the top finding from 33-b) plus the three smaller 33-b findings (tdm int passthrough, youngs/bsa message rendering, ClassificationReport numpy scalars).

Work Log:
- REAL DEFECT FIXED (fail-first scratch/probe_roc_auc_34.py): evaluate_model's binary branch used roc_auc_score(y_true, proba[:, 1]) -- column 1 ASSUMED to be the positive class's probability. roc_auc_score treats y_true's sorted-LAST label as positive; a conformant sklearn estimator's proba columns follow its own sorted classes_ so the assumption held, but a custom estimator is free to expose classes_ in its own order -- and a PERFECT classifier over {'high','low'} with classes_=['low','high'] (col 0 = P('low')) reported roc_auc = 0.0, silently inverted (probe assertion fired exactly as predicted). Fix in src/pharmaml/ml/evaluation.py: locate the positive-class column through the estimator's own classes_ when it exposes one (pos_label = np.unique(y_true)[-1], column found by membership; no match -> the sklearn-convention column 1 fallback), with a comment carrying the fail-first story. Probe now passes: non-conformant perfect classifier 1.0, conformant sklearn 1.0 unchanged.
- REGRESSION TESTS (TestEvaluationEdgeCases, +5): the inversion case (roc_auc == 1.0 where it was 0.0), conformant-estimator invariance, the unrelated-classes_ fallback semantics pinned (column 1 IS the score vector used -- a wrong 'use column 0' heuristic would report 0.0), the single-class-y_true None path, and plain-scalar labels. One test-authoring correction mid-round: the first mismatched-classes design assumed roc_auc_score raises on label-set mismatch -- it does not for binary (any score vector is legal); redesigned to pin the actual fallback semantics instead.
- 33-b FINDING #4 FIXED: ClassificationReport.labels carried numpy scalars -- labels = sorted(np.unique(concatenate(...).tolist())) put .tolist() INSIDE np.unique's argument, so np.unique re-wrapped it as an ndarray and sorted() yielded np.int64/np.str_ entries. Fix: .tolist() moved OUTSIDE. 33-b's doctest had routed around the trap with [int(v) for v in report.labels] -- still passes unchanged; new test asserts plain python scalars (no np.generic).
- 33-b FINDING #2 FIXED: tdm_trough_adjustment's clamp assigned adjusted = min_dose verbatim -- an int min_dose passed through as int, violating the -> float contract (min_dose=2000 returned 2000, not 2000.0). Fix: float(min_dose); module-doctest gained the int-clamp pin (2000 -> 2000.0); regression test asserts value AND isinstance(float).
- 33-b FINDING #3 FIXED: youngs_rule rendered the age pre-cast ("got 15") while bsa_mosteller (via validate_positive's cast) rendered post-cast ("got 300.0") -- an inconsistency inside one module. Standardised on the POST-cast rendering (the validate_positive family's dominant convention): youngs' message now floats the age ("got 15.0"); doctest pin updated, bounds test gains match="got 15.0".
- NOTEBOOK IMPACT CHECKED: complete_pk_workflow.ipynb uses youngs_rule(6.0, 250.0) (valid range) and tdm_trough_adjustment with plain calls -- no error-message or int-clamp pins anywhere, so no notebook re-execution needed (verified by grepping sources+outputs).

Stage Summary:
- Granularity: 3 levels -- level1 {crossover, clone} per offspring; geometry {the 7 scaffold-hop buckets, splice mode degenerates to 1} per recombination; mutation family {mode-primary, character} per offspring (uniform mode: no draw).
- Credit rule: per-attempt push into a 20-outcome window; reward = (valid offspring ? score : 0.0) - mid_parent; a drawn operator whose own product was discarded (returned None/fell back) takes the null reward 0.0 - mid_parent; credit = mean(window), empty window = 0.0 (never NaN).
- Selection rule: p_i = floor + (1-k*floor)*softmax(credit_i/T), floor = 1/(k*5), T = 0.1; single rng.random() draw per selection; full determinism proven cross-process.
- API: GeneticOptimizer(..., operator_selection="uniform"|"adaptive", aos_window=20, aos_temperature=0.1) with DataValidationError guards; scaffold_hop_crossover(..., geometry_weights=None) with ValueError guards (private _scaffold_hop_core returns (child, geometry) for the trace); metadata gains "operator_selection" + "operator_stats" {level1, geometry, mutation} only in adaptive mode.
- Pin-safety: default path keeps the exact current branches (857/858/861) and the exact single candidates[randrange] draw; metadata untouched in uniform mode (probe C.2 hashes); ~18 new tests + 2 doctest pins + CLI --adaptive-operators; notebook A/B demo deferred to a notebook round.

FEATURES.PY API CONTRACT (binding for agents A and C):
- Module: src/pharmaml/chem/features.py, exported via pharmaml.chem (__init__ + __all__ alphabetical).
- FEATURE_FAMILIES: tuple[str, ...] = ("descriptors", "atompair_count", "ecfp", "avalon_count", "rdkit_fingerprint", "morgan_full", "morgan_scaffold"); FAMILY_PREFIXES maps family -> column prefix: descriptors->"desc_", atompair_count->"apc_bit_", ecfp->"ecfp_bit_", avalon_count->"avalon_count_", rdkit_fingerprint->"rdkit_bit_", morgan_full->"morgan_full_bit_", morgan_scaffold->"morgan_scaffold_bit_".
- Bit sizes: apc/ecfp/rdkit/morgan_full/morgan_scaffold = 2048, avalon = 512 (module constants ATOMPAIR_BITS=2048, ECFP_BITS=2048, AVALON_BITS=512, RDKIT_FP_BITS=2048, MORGAN_BITS=2048, MORGAN_RADIUS=2, ATOMPAIR... fold sparse counts by idx % bits).
- @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) FeatureReport: smiles: list[str] (valid, row order), dropped: list[tuple[int, str]] ((row, smiles) unparseable/failed), families: dict[str, int] (family -> n columns produced); properties total_columns: int, n_valid: int.
- compute_feature_frame(smiles: Sequence[str], families: Iterable[str] = FEATURE_FAMILIES) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, FeatureReport]: frame columns = family prefixes in FEATURE_FAMILIES order (only requested families), one row per VALID molecule (rows dropped entirely on failure, recorded in report), float dtype, NaN preserved (no fillna here); ValueError on unknown family / empty families / empty smiles input. Descriptors family = rdMolDescriptors.Properties(GetAvailableProperties()) columns named desc_<prop>. Murcko via GetScaffoldForMol (empty scaffold -> zero rows, NOT dropped). Deps: rdkit+numpy+pandas; NO datamol, NO mordred.
- family_of_column(column: str) -> str (inverse prefix map; ValueError on unknown prefix).
- rank_features(frame: pd.DataFrame, target: Sequence[float] | None = None, *, method: str = "auto", task: str = "auto", random_state: int = 42) -> pd.Series: importance per column, sorted DESCENDING, index=frame.columns. method in {"auto","random_forest","lightgbm","variance"} ("auto" -> "variance" if target is None else "lightgbm" if importable else "random_forest"); task in {"auto","classification","regression"} ("auto" -> classification iff target non-numeric OR <=2 unique values). X = frame.fillna(0).astype(float); RF = RandomForest{Classifier,Regressor}(n_estimators=200, random_state=rs); LGBM = LGBM{Classifier,Regressor}(n_estimators=200, random_state=rs, verbosity=-1) - LightGBM strictly OPTIONAL (skip/ImportError->fallback when missing). Variance = frame.fillna(0).astype(float).var(axis=0) (constant cols -> 0.0). Length mismatch target/frame -> ValueError. NaN/±inf in target -> ValueError (guard BEFORE fit).
- select_top_features(frame: pd.DataFrame, scores: pd.Series, k: int, *, median_prefilter: bool = True, method: str = "") -> FeatureSelection: @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True) FeatureSelection{scores: pd.Series, selected: list[str], family_counts: dict[str,int], method: str}. median_prefilter=True: within EACH family keep cols with score >= family median ( rar layer 1 ), then top-K by score (ties -> frame column order); k<=0 ValueError; k>=len -> all candidates in score order. selected respects the two-layer contract. scores index must equal frame columns (ValueError otherwise).
- selection_metadata(selection: FeatureSelection, report: FeatureReport, *, k: int, families: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]: {"selected_features": list, "descriptor_names": list[str] (desc_* stripped), "fingerprint_sizes": {"ecfp":2048,"rdkit_fingerprint":2048,"morgan_full":2048,"morgan_scaffold":2048,"avalon_count":512,"atompair_count":2048}, "family_counts": dict, "families_computed": report.families, "k_requested": k, "method": selection.method, "n_molecules": report.n_valid, "dropped": [[row, smiles], ...], "total_features": report.total_columns} - JSON-ready (json.dump with default=str safe).
- Style: full numpydoc docstrings with Parameters/Returns/Raises/Notes, >=6 doctests using SMALL family subsets (families=("descriptors",) or ("ecfp","avalon_count")) for speed, deterministic (random_state everywhere), mypy --strict clean, ruff clean, pin-format matches src/pharmaml/chem/descriptors.py. Tests in tests/test_features.py: FAIL-FIRST (red run witnessed in the agent's log), cover families/counts/dropped/rankers (synthetic frame with KNOWN informative column - not SMILES-derived for rank determinism)/two-layer selection/k edges/metadata keys/ValueErrors; total-columns > 10,000 contract test on the full 7 families over the 10-row examples/data/ligand_library.csv (8 valid).
- GUI WIRING (agent C) calls ONLY this public API + pharmaml.utils.io.write_table; exports mirror the rar: selected-features CSV = SMILES + (target if present) + selected columns in rank order; metadata JSON via selection_metadata.

- *** THE OOM HUNT (the round's real engineering story) ***: the first full test-class run was OOM-KILLED (exit 137, RSS spike +1.4 GB in 2 s). Bisection: single tests passed; the residual-classifier test alone reliably died; direct in-process reproduction was 421 MB — so the explosion was in the GUI render path. ROOT CAUSE (two stacked bugs): (1) qsar_classification.csv's LAST column is compound_id (420 unique string IDs); both dataset cards defaulted target = last column, so the run trained a 420-CLASS classifier on row IDs; (2) plot_confusion_matrix had NO large-matrix guard — figsize grew linearly with n (420 classes -> a 464-INCH canvas) plus n^2 = 176k per-cell text artists => GBs of allocation. FIXES: (a) new default_target_column(frame) pure helper — walks from the right, skips the SMILES column and unique-per-row OBJECT columns (numeric all-unique stays: it is a legitimate regression target); both _ml_load_path and _dl_load_path preselect it (and _ml_load_path's task inference now uses the CHOSEN target, not the last column); (b) plot_confusion_matrix guard — annotated only when n <= 50, figure size capped at min(n, 12) cells, tick fontsize shrinks beyond the limit, title gains " — N classes, cells unannotated". After the fixes the whole DL class runs in ~31 s with no OOM (the 420-class run still completes and renders a plain heat-map if a user insists on an ID target).

Verdict: unwieldy fronts are real, the feature is warranted.
- LIBRARY (pareto.py): ParetoFront.crowding_distance() — textbook NSGA-II: per objective sort by (value, index), boundary positions marked +inf (the trade-off corners), interiors accumulate (next - prev)/(max - min); a no-spread objective (max == min) contributes 0 to everyone (crowding measures spread; a lone member or fully degenerate front returns 0.0s — documented). ParetoFront.prune(keep) — selection ranked by (-distance, leaderboard rank), re-emitted in leaderboard order (the front's standing convention); keep >= len returns self (frozen, immutable); keep < 1 raises DataValidationError. New field n_front (default None — every existing constructor call unaffected). KEY DESIGN DISCOVERY: pairwise dominance cannot change with membership, so a pruned front keeps every member's ORIGINAL dominates counts (the audit survives the cut) — no recompute needed. __str__ honesty rule pinned: a pruned front reports the ORIGINAL non-dominated count ("7 of 36") plus the prune suffix ("pruned to the 3 most isolated of 7 by crowding distance") — claiming the pruned count as non-dominated would be factually wrong. to_dataframe() gains the crowding column.
- CLI: --pareto-keep N (with --pareto) — prunes the printed front; actionable typed errors for missing --pareto and keep < 1 (the --pareto-plot convention); module usage example + handler docstring updated. Live smoke test: the seed-7 druglike run printed "pruned to the 4 most isolated of 15 by crowding distance" with the corners at inf.

## Round 204 — the feature-recalculation roundtrip: the factory's stored metadata replayed on new molecules, v1.2.118 shipped (2026-11-07)

The owner's catalog continuation directive: *"add a section to use the
metadata stored by the feature factory to recalculate the selected
features."* The selection metadata the factory's Save-JSON button
writes (`selection_metadata`: selected features in rank order, the
family ledger, the fingerprint sizes, K, method) is now a first-class
REPLAY input — the QSAR workflow's "apply the frozen feature set"
step, one library function + one card.

The library arm — `pharmaml.chem.features.recalculate_selected_features(smiles,
metadata, n_jobs, progress)` — replays a recorded selection against a
fresh SMILES batch: only the families the recorded columns need are
computed (a descriptors-only selection never touches the seventeen
fingerprint families — the efficiency promise has its own test), the
result carries exactly the recorded columns in the recorded rank
order, and `n_jobs`/`progress` pass straight through to
`compute_feature_frame`. The ledger keys the metadata itself carries
are cross-checked BEFORE any chemistry runs, so a stale file from a
different build fails loudly instead of silently recomputing a
drifted vocabulary: `fingerprint_sizes` contradictions (recorded bits
vs this build's), `families_computed` inconsistencies (a selected
column whose family was never computed), unknown column prefixes,
duplicate/empty entries, and features that no longer exist in this
build's frame (an RDKit property that vanished) are all honest
ValueError stops with the exact story. Exported through
`pharmaml.chem` beside its sibling `selection_metadata`.

The playground card — *Feature recalculation (from metadata)*
(Chemistry, row 13, span 2) — carries the round-202 guarantees by
construction: a one-line subtitle, the **Descriptors & features**
workflow badge (the pipeline is now 5 steps — canonical-SMILES →
inspector → factory → RECALCULATION → similarity scan; the other four
cards' badges renumbered automatically from the registry), and
sample-data ready: `examples/data/selection_metadata.json`, a REAL
variance-ranked top-24 (ecfp + descriptors, 22 + 2 columns) written
by the factory's own metadata saver over eight drug-like molecules,
roundtrip-verified before commit. Three adoption paths: the bundled
example, any saved JSON file, or **the factory's current in-session
selection** (no file round-trip at all — the relay builds the metadata
exactly the way Save-JSON writes it). The render is the value matrix
— molecules x recorded features, the first six columns as live tree
headings (the factory tree's mirror: rows are molecules here,
columns are the frozen features) — and Save writes CSV / Excel
(.xlsx) / TSV / Markdown / JSON / HTML through the standard table
dialog (the Excel guarantee rides free).

Verification: `tests/test_feature_recalculation.py` — 30 tests (15
library incl. the value-parity cross-check against a direct compute,
the dropped-molecule report, the progress callback and every loud
stop; 2 example-file honesty tests; 13 GUI under Xvfb incl. the badge
text "Descriptors & features · step 4/5", the three adoption paths,
the run+render, the stale-metadata error surfacing through the job
poller's dialog, and the xlsx save round-trip). Regression battery

## Round 205 — the heavy-work safety kit: the collapse report answered (stop button, memory watchdog, batch guard, n_jobs cap), v1.2.119 shipped (2026-11-07)

The owner's report (IM, verbatim): *"Playground.py collapses during
heavy work."* Diagnosis first, on the box's own evidence: this sandbox
runs 4 GB / 2 cores with ~1.6 GB available once the dev server and
browser pool settle; dmesg carries TWO recorded OOM kills of python
(1.1 GB and 0.95 GB anon-RSS); and the tune path's loky probe showed
**7 worker processes** for one `n_jobs=4` GridSearchCV call — every
worker a full interpreter holding a dataset copy. The collapse mode:
heavy work outruns the RAM → the kernel kills the biggest process —
the Tk app itself — and the window vanishes with every loaded input.
The reproduction harness (`scratch/stress_playground.py`, real app
under Xvfb, real card flows through the real worker-thread path)
closed the loop: before the fix there was NO stop channel at all (a
`rg -i cancel` over playground.py finds only dialog Cancel buttons),
no memory arithmetic anywhere, and n_jobs allowed up to 32 loky
workers on a box that cannot feed two.

The fix, in two arms:

* **The cooperative-stop channel (pharmaml)** —
  `pharmaml.exceptions.JobCancelled`, raised at every checkpoint loop
  when the progress callback answers `False`: the feature factory's
  molecule-batch boundary (and therefore the recalculation replay,
  which passes the callback through), BOTH progressive table readers'
  chunk boundaries (the stop propagates as itself, never wrapped into
  DataValidationError), and both CV leaderboards' completed rows
  (compare_models / benchmark_feature_families). Callbacks returning
  None or truthy never cancel — every historical callback and mock is
  byte-identical.
* **The app machinery (playground)** — the status-bar **Stop button**
  (enabled exactly while busy; a checkpoint-less job gets the honest
  "no checkpoints" label; a stop lands as "cancelled after X s" + an
  info dialog naming the reason, never a red traceback); the **live
  memory watchdog** riding the standing 150 ms poll (job ceiling =
  launch RSS + 75% of launch-time MemAvailable, plus a 256 MB system
  floor; both trip the same stop flag BEFORE the kernel would strike);
  the **pre-flight batch guard** (factory + recalculation cards
  estimate molecules × columns × 3 copies × 8 bytes and refuse with
  their own arithmetic when it cannot fit half the available memory;
  off-Linux the guards stand down); and the **ML n_jobs memory cap**
  (768 MB of available memory per loky worker, the reduction riding
  the job label — "n_jobs 4→2 (memory cap)" — never silent).

Verification: the stress driver's six phases all green — mid-job Stop
("cancelled after 3 s", checkpoint 100/237 named), the same job
unstopped completing (231 × 27,759 frame in 7 s — a stop never
poisons the next job), the watchdog trip ("stopped by memory ceiling
after 1 s"), the guard refusal with full arithmetic, the cap maths,
and the recalculation + xgboost regressions (the cap engaging live on
this box: "training xgboost — n_jobs 2→1 (memory cap)"). Focused
batteries: test_job_safety 26 green; recalc+csv 87 green; the four
touched modules' doctests green; ml_pipeline+interpret xdist exit 0;
TestGuiUnderXvfb 22 + TestFeatureFactoryGuiUnderXvfb 7 green;
`--self-test` green under Xvfb. Full-suite runs were OOM-killed by the
BOX itself (peer session's 1.8 GB stdin-workers were resident) — the
focused-battery convention of rounds 203-204 applied instead.
